# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: the walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`, `observatory-cli replay` over
one captured session, an empty board that starts) is integrated on `mission/observatory-v1`
(2026-10-23). Each later milestone deepens one area from it.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: N`: `2027` on the S fixture
   (`2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl`, the mapper knows no kind yet), `0` from the M0 fixture
   onward.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to `BACKLOG.md` as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs or GitHub issues
  (rule 14; owner decision 2026-10-22 at mission approval).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

### VAL-PROC-038: No email address and no `/home/user` path remains in any committed fixture file from the `m0` integration onward
At the `m0` integration commit and at every later integration commit `<sha>`, `git grep -I -nE '[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}' <sha> -- fixtures/streams/ | grep -v '@example.invalid' | wc -l` prints 0 and `git grep -I -nF '/home/user' <sha> -- fixtures/streams/ | wc -l` prints 0, over every tracked file under `fixtures/streams/` (the S fixture `2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` with its `.children/`, `.settings.json` and `.capture.json`, redacted before the M0 freeze, and the M0 capture `2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.*`, including the GitHub noreply address the S root carried at the `s` integration). The redaction is a deterministic rewrite of the same length where possible (for example `user@example.invalid`, `/home/user`), so `wc -l` of each redacted `.jsonl` equals the line count of its original (the original is out of the repository; VAL-PROC-039). Fail if either count is non-zero at any of these integration commits, or if a fixture file's line count differs from its original's (owner decision 2026-10-23, PII rule for fixtures; AGENTS.md "Raw session JSONL may contain secrets"; RULES rule 13 for the shared `fixtures/streams/` path).
Tool: git
Evidence: terminal-output(the two grep counts per integration sha from m0 onward, 0 each), terminal-output(wc -l of each redacted .jsonl next to wc -l of its original)

### VAL-PROC-039: Each fixture's `.capture.json` records the redaction with per-file hashes, and the decision file names the same hashes and the location of the originals
For each committed fixture (`2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s` from the `m0` integration commit, `2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0` from its integration commit), `jq -r '.redaction.script' <fixture>.capture.json` prints the name of the redaction script, and `jq -r '.redaction.files[] | "\(.path) \(.original_sha256) \(.redacted_sha256)"' <fixture>.capture.json` prints one row for every tracked `.jsonl` (root and `.children/*.jsonl`) and `.settings.json` of that fixture, each with two 64-hex-character hashes (the sidecar itself and the golden `.events.json` are produced after redaction and carry no row). For every row, `shasum -a 256 fixtures/streams/<path>` equals `redacted_sha256`. A decision file `docs/decisions/D-NNN-*.md` recording the PII rule (owner decision 2026-10-23) names the out-of-repo directory that holds the originals, lists the same `original_sha256` and `redacted_sha256` pairs for the same paths (`diff <(jq -r '.redaction.files[] | "\(.original_sha256) \(.redacted_sha256)"' <fixture>.capture.json | sort) <(grep -oE '[0-9a-f]{64}' docs/decisions/D-NNN-*.md | paste - - | sort)` is empty, or an equivalent comparison pasted), and states that byte offsets are computed against the redacted file because that is the one the store indexes. The originals are never committed: `git log --all --diff-filter=A --format=%h -- '*<original basename>*'` outside `fixtures/streams/` prints nothing. Fail if `.redaction` is absent, a tracked `.jsonl` or `.settings.json` has no row, a hash is not 64 hex characters, a `redacted_sha256` does not match the committed bytes, the decision file is missing or lists different hashes, or the out-of-repo location is not named (owner decision 2026-10-23; architecture §4.2 `.capture.json` header; SPEC §3 "Common" fixture rule; RULES rule 7).
Tool: shell
Evidence: terminal-output(jq .redaction.script and the files rows per fixture), terminal-output(shasum -a 256 of each committed path next to its redacted_sha256), file(the decision file lines with the originals' location and the hash pairs), terminal-output(the diff of the two hash lists, empty)

### VAL-PROC-040: Replay of a redacted fixture yields one event per line and every `SourcePtr` byte offset slices the redacted file to a line of the event's raw type
For each committed fixture (`2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl` from the `m0` integration commit, `2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl` from its integration commit), the count of event lines printed by `cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<fixture>.jsonl` (lines before the final `unknown events: N` summary; VAL-SKEL-005) equals `wc -l < fixtures/streams/<fixture>.jsonl`. Then, using whichever surface exposes `byte_offset` and `byte_len` at that milestone (the golden `<fixture>.events.json` at `m0` and later, `replay --json`, or `inspect <event-id>`; VAL-SKEL-009, VAL-MAP-017), a loop over every event of the root file slices the committed redacted file with `dd if=fixtures/streams/<path> bs=1 skip=<byte_offset> count=<byte_len> 2>/dev/null`: every slice parses as JSON (`jq -e .type` exits 0), and for every event that carries `raw_type` (all events of the S fixture; the `Unknown` events of M0) the slice's `.type` equals that `raw_type`. The loop reports the number of events checked and the number of mismatches, pasted; offsets are computed against the redacted bytes, never against the original (owner decision 2026-10-23: "compute all byte offsets against the redacted file, since that is the one the store indexes"; invariants I3, I4; architecture §4.2). Fail if the event count differs from the line count, any slice does not parse, any `raw_type` differs from the sliced line's `type`, or the loop was run on fewer than all events of the root file.
Tool: cli
Evidence: terminal-output(replay event-line count next to wc -l per fixture), terminal-output(the loop script and its two counts, mismatches 0), terminal-output(one pasted slice next to its event's raw_type)

### VAL-PROC-041: `gitleaks detect --no-git --source fixtures/streams` reports no leaks on the redacted fixtures at every integration commit
At each of the seven integration commits `<sha>` (`git checkout --detach <sha>` in a scratch worktree, or the worktree at integration time), `gitleaks detect --no-git --no-banner --redact --source fixtures/streams` exits 0 and its output contains `no leaks found`; for the fixtures redacted under the PII rule (`2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.*` from `m0` onward, `2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.*` from its integration), the `.capture.json` `gitleaks` field (VAL-SKEL-014, VAL-MAP-002) carries a `clean` result whose date is on or after the redaction, and the fixture-adding commit on `wt/<m>` is dated after that scan (the scan runs on the redacted bytes before the commit, not on the original). The same rule applies to every future fixture under `fixtures/streams/`. Fail on exit code 1 or any finding at any integration commit, a `gitleaks` field dated before the redaction, or a fixture committed before its scan (owner decision 2026-10-23 "Run gitleaks on the redacted fixture before committing; same rule for every future fixture"; VAL-PROC-007 covers the `s`/`m0` fixture scan and the history scan; SPEC §3 "Common").
Tool: shell
Evidence: terminal-output(gitleaks detect exit code and summary line at each of the seven integration shas), terminal-output(jq .gitleaks of each redacted fixture's .capture.json next to the fixture-adding commit date from git log)

### VAL-PROC-042: `log-tool-call.sh` logs the first 200 characters of a `Script` call's script and `null` for other tools
From the integration commit that lands the change (named by a `docs/decisions/D-NNN-*.md`, VAL-PROC-022) and at every later integration commit, `.factory/hooks/log-tool-call.sh` writes a `script` field in each build-log line: for a `Script` tool call it holds the first 200 characters of `tool_input.script`; for any other tool it is `null`. Pipe a second payload with `tool_name` `Execute` and a `tool_input.command`: `tail -1 ... | jq -r '.script'` prints `null` and the previously logged fields (`command`, `file_path`, `summary`, `exit_code`) are unchanged in shape. Fail if the field is absent, longer or shorter than 200 for the 300-character input, non-null for a non-Script call, the hook exits non-zero, or the change landed without a decision file (owner decision 2026-10-23 at the S → M0 boundary; SPEC §2 `log-tool-call.sh`; RULES rule 17; VAL-PROC-023 for the build-log layout).
Tool: shell
Evidence: terminal-output(the two piped payloads, hook exit codes, and the jq outputs 200 and null), file(the decision file name), git-log(git log --format=%h -- .factory/hooks/log-tool-call.sh at the integration sha)
